result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 8 pass / 0 fail.

I added `app/Support/redirects.ts`, which exports `DEFAULT_LOGIN_REDIRECT` (`/dashboard`, matching the `requireGuest` destination in `routes/web.ts`) and `sameAppPath()` — a helper that first normalises a candidate the way a browser's URL parser would (stripping tab/LF/CR, folding backslashes to forward slashes) and then returns the value only when it is rooted at a single `/`, yielding `null` for absolute URLs with a scheme, protocol-relative `//host` values, backslash variants like `/\evil.example`, control-character smuggling, and non-strings. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts` now runs every attacker-controlled `redirect` through it: `show()` passes only a same-app path (or `''`) into the login page's hidden field, and `store()` picks the first same-app path among the request body and query values, falling back to `DEFAULT_LOGIN_REDIRECT` when neither qualifies — so a rejected redirect still signs the user in and just lands them on the default page, while a wrong password still throws the same 422 as before. `tests/LoginController.test.ts` covers the helper's accept/reject cases plus the four HTTP behaviours (returns to `/posts/3/edit`, defaults without a redirect, ignores off-site redirects, wrong password still 422), and I noted the new `app/Support/` directory in the README's project-structure list.
